audit.title: Chainlink ACE Overview
audit.contentType: developer documentation / product overview (conceptual landing page)
audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual overview of Chainlink ACE that leads with a crisp, liftable definition and uses question-phrased headings that match how developers query. Its strongest GEO asset is clarity and answer-first structure; its biggest opportunities are near-zero machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no `dateModified` in `<head>`) and thin concrete specifics — 13 numerals but **0 with units** and no supported-network/version/limit data. Honest verdict: a strong prose page held back by missing schema and quantitative detail, both fixable without touching the voice.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL and dates
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD carrying `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-07-17` (already shown in body), `about: "Chainlink ACE"`, and `url`/`mainEntityOfPage` set to the canonical `https://docs.chain.link/ace`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and a visible freshness signal are direct E-E-A-T/trust inputs engines use to select and attribute sources.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics with units
recommendations.issue: 0 of 13 numerals carry units; no networks, counts, or limits.
recommendations.change: State the supported EVM chains by name, the number of pre-built policies in the library, and the three named APIs' functions (Coordinator, Evaluation, Reporting). Replace vague "across every EVM chain" with the actual supported-chain set.
recommendations.why: Quantitative, named specifics are among the highest-lift changes for retrieval and citation.

recommendations.title: Add a summary table of the three managers
recommendations.issue: three managers described in prose bullets; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: Add a 3-row table — Manager | Interface (UI/API) | Purpose — mirroring Policy/Identity/Reporting Manager. Add a second small table for delegated vs self-signing.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract discrete, comparable facts and build justified answers.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative external citations for compliance terms
recommendations.where: "What problems does ACE solve?" and "Key features"
recommendations.change: Link "sanctions screening" to the TRM Wallet Screening source, and "accredited investor"/KYC/AML to their canonical definitions or standards.
recommendations.why: Inline primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Lead the "What is ACE?" section with a one-line canonical two-layer statement
recommendations.issue: current lead is good but the two-layer split is spread across a sentence + two subsections.
recommendations.change: Keep the existing sentence but ensure the first liftable line names both layers explicitly: "ACE has two layers — onchain smart contracts (PolicyEngine, Cross-Chain Identity) and the ACE Platform (Policy, Identity, Reporting Managers)."
recommendations.why: A single self-contained sentence resists parametric substitution when the section is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Add one minimal integration snippet
recommendations.where: near the "How it works" example or a link-out to `ace-compatible`
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; agents have no anchor for what a "protected function" looks like.
recommendations.change: Add a short, language-tagged Solidity snippet showing a function guarded by the PolicyEngine call, or surface the first snippet from the ACE-compatible guide.
recommendations.why: Even one complete, tagged snippet improves agent parsing and grounds the concept.

antiPatterns: Body-only freshness: "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" is present but not machine-exposed via metadata.
One unresolved media reference: "(Image: Image)" placeholder in "How it works" carries no alt text or caption for engines to read.
No marketing fluff, keyword stuffing, or walls of prose detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Canonical URL and og/twitter tags are typically template/site-level; fix at the docs framework layer, not per page.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` on the next run — head metadata "could not be verified" here, so the schema/canonical findings rest solely on the served-HTML scan.
